Let
\[
q(\lambda)=\prod_{j=1}^3\frac{\lambda-r_j}{\lambda+r_j},
\qquad r_j=\alpha_j^{-1}>0.
\]
Scale \(\lambda=3t\), so \(t\in[1/3,3]\). We minimize
\[
\max_{1/3\le t\le 3}|q(t)|.
\]

The optimal roots are reciprocal about \(t=1\), so write
\[
q_B(t)=\frac{(t-1)(t^2-(B-1)t+1)}{(t+1)(t^2+(B-1)t+1)}
=\frac{t^3-Bt^2+Bt-1}{t^3+Bt^2+Bt+1},
\]
where \(B>3\). Put
\[
F_B(t)=\frac{1+q_B(t)}{1-q_B(t)}
=\frac{t(t^2+B)}{Bt^2+1}.
\]
Since \(q=(F-1)/(F+1)\), extrema of \(q_B\) occur where
\[
F_B'(t)=0.
\]
A direct differentiation gives
\[
F_B'(t)=0
\iff
Bt^4+(3-B^2)t^2+B=0.
\]

At the minimax value, the four alternating extrema occur at
\[
t=\frac13,\quad \frac1v,\quad v,\quad 3,
\]
with values
\[
-\rho,\quad \rho,\quad -\rho,\quad \rho.
\]
The condition \(q_B(3)=\rho\) and \(q_B(v)=-\rho\), with \(v\) a double root of \(q_B(t)+\rho\), gives
\[
q_B(t)+\rho=(1+\rho)(t-\tfrac13)(t-v)^2.
\]
Comparing coefficients yields
\[
v^2=\frac{3(1-\rho)}{1+\rho},
\qquad
B=v^2+\frac{2v}{3}
=\frac{6}{v}+\frac1{v^2}.
\]
Thus
\[
3v^4+2v^3-18v-3=0.
\]
Eliminating \(v\) using \(v^2=3(1-\rho)/(1+\rho)\) gives
\[
16\rho^4-8\rho^3+24\rho^2-32\rho+1=0.
\]

It remains to justify optimality. For any candidate \(q\), define
\[
F=\frac{1+q}{1-q}.
\]
Every such \(F\) has the form
\[
F(t)=\frac{t(t^2+b)}{at^2+c}
\qquad(a,b,c>0).
\]
For two candidates \(F,F_B\), the difference \(F-F_B\), after clearing the positive denominators, has numerator \(t\) times a quadratic polynomial in \(t^2\). Hence it has at most two positive zeros unless the functions are identical. If another candidate had smaller uniform norm than \(q_B\), then at the four alternating points
\[
\frac13<\frac1v<v<3
\]
the signs of \(q-q_B\), equivalently \(F-F_B\), would alternate, forcing at least three positive zeros, impossible. Therefore this equioscillating candidate is optimal.

The relevant root is the small positive one. Indeed, for
\[
p(t)=16t^4-8t^3+24t^2-32t+1,
\]
we have
\[
p(1/32)>0,\qquad p(1/30)<0,
\]
and \(p'(t)<0\) on \((1/32,1/30)\), so there is exactly one root there.

Therefore
\[
\boxed{\rho_*=\operatorname{Root}\!\left(16t^4-8t^3+24t^2-32t+1;\left(\frac1{32},\frac1{30}\right)\right)}.
\]
